title: Nodding Head Emoji 🙂‍↕️ Meaning: Yes, Agreed, Noted
description: 🙂‍↕️ is a nodding head: “yes,” “agreed” or “got it.” See how it differs from a thumbs up, how it is used online, and why some phones show it as two symbols.
summary: 🙂‍↕️ is a smiling face nodding up and down. It means “yes.” People use it to agree, accept, confirm they understood, or show approval. It is a warmer, more personal alternative to 👍, and online it also conveys knowing, satisfied agreement.
meaning: A nod is the simplest way to say yes without speaking, and this emoji puts it on the keyboard. Its official name calls it a head shaking vertically, but everyone reads it as nodding. In reply to a question it is a plain affirmative: “Still on for lunch?” “🙂‍↕️.” The gentle smile makes the yes friendly without the excitement of an exclamation mark.

It also means “I hear you.” In conversation, people nod to show they are following along, and 🙂‍↕️ does that in text. Sent while a friend explains a problem or lays out a plan, it says “go on, I'm with you.” This listening nod is distinct from agreement. It acknowledges without necessarily endorsing, which is useful and occasionally ambiguous.

Approval is the third sense. Replying 🙂‍↕️ to a good idea, a nice outfit or a well-made point is a nod of respect, the text version of “mm-hm, that's right.” On social media the nod often turns smug or emphatic: “me agreeing with my own bad decisions 🙂‍↕️.” Fans use it under posts they strongly co-sign, sometimes in rows.

One reason people like it is the trouble with 👍. A thumbs up strikes some readers, especially younger ones, as curt or passive-aggressive. A smiling nod carries the same “yes, okay” with more warmth. The emoji came out in the 2023 release with its head-shaking partner and reached phones in 2024, so support on older devices is incomplete.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It answers yes-or-no questions, confirms plans and shows you are following a long story. It is softer than “yes.” and friendlier than “k.” When someone asks for your opinion on something important, add words, because a nod alone may look like you did not give it much thought.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: As a reaction, it means “understood” or “agreed,” and it is a good substitute for 👍 in teams where the thumb feels abrupt. It suits acknowledging instructions and seconding a suggestion. For approvals that need a record, such as budgets or sign-offs, write “approved” so nobody has to interpret a nod.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: It marks emphatic agreement with a relatable post and appears in captions as a self-satisfied nod. Music content uses it for head-bobbing to a beat. It is commonly set against 🙂‍↔️ in jokes about saying yes to one thing and no to another, or about contradicting yourself.

contexts.label: Around the world
contexts.body: Nodding means yes in most places where this emoji is used, but not everywhere. In Bulgaria the usual meanings of nodding and shaking are reversed, and in Greece and Turkey a single upward tilt of the head can mean no. A word alongside the emoji avoids confusion with international contacts.

examples.text: “Can you grab milk on the way home?” 🙂‍↕️
So we split the cost three ways, right? 🙂‍↕️

examples.meaning: Nodding along to the music in approval.
Agreeing firmly with something said in the sender's favor.

examples.text: Me when the waiter asks if I want more bread 🙂‍↕️
Got it, I'll send the file by noon 🙂‍↕️

combos.meaning: Clear agreement; yes, and it's all good.
Bobbing your head to a song.
Total agreement with what was said.
Yes and no at once; undecided, or joking about mixed feelings.

confusedWith.difference: 🙂‍↔️ shakes left and right for “no.” 🙂‍↕️ nods up and down for “yes.” They are drawn from the same face and differ only in the direction of movement, which makes them easy to swap by accident.
👍 is a quick approval or acknowledgment and can feel terse to some readers. 🙂‍↕️ shows a face, so it comes across as more attentive and personal. Both mean yes; the nod is the gentler one.
🙇 lowers the whole upper body in a deep bow of apology, gratitude or respect. 🙂‍↕️ is only a nod of agreement. A bow asks for or acknowledges something serious; a nod just says yes.

avoid: Do not use it as your only confirmation for something that needs a clear written yes, such as a contract or payment.
Avoid it when the recipient's device may be old enough to split it into a smiley and an arrow.
Skip the lone nod when a friend shares something emotional, because it can read as half-listening.
design: A slightly smiling yellow face caught mid-nod, with motion marks or faint duplicate outlines above and below to show up-and-down movement. It is a joined sequence of the slightly smiling face and the up-down arrow, and unsupported systems show 🙂 followed by ↕️. Some messaging apps animate the nod when the emoji is sent alone.

faqs.a: Yes. It shows a nod, which means agreement, acceptance or acknowledgment. Depending on the conversation, it can be “yes, I will,” “I agree,” or “I'm following what you're saying.”

faqs.q: Why does my phone show 🙂 and ↕️ separately?
faqs.a: The nodding head is built by joining those two characters. It was introduced in 2023, and operating systems or apps that have not added it since cannot merge the pair, so each piece is displayed separately.

It is often received more warmly. Some people find a thumbs up dismissive, while a smiling nod feels engaged. For quick acknowledgments both work, and the nod is a good choice when you want to seem friendly.

Strong or smug agreement. People use it to co-sign a relatable statement, to nod along to music, or to show they are pleased with a choice. It is frequently paired with its opposite, 🙂‍↔️, for contrast.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 🙂‍↕️ and 🙂‍↔️?
faqs.a: 🙂‍↕️ nods vertically and means yes. 🙂‍↔️ shakes horizontally and means no. Check the motion lines: above and below the face for a nod, on either side for a shake.
